reasoning: Kept three narrow clarifications not already covered by the skill: interpreting book-framed clues, preferring a shared constituency when context supports it, and preserving canonical plural taxonomic names. Inserted each beside the most relevant existing guidance, outside the protected section. Each clarification is supported by one source patch. [optimizer-ranked: selected 2/3 edits]

edits.target: For direct definition or trivia clues, treat the description as a fill-in target and return the conventional term or category called for by the whole clue, including after elliptical wording such as “one of these.” Match the requested grammatical number; when the answer is a singular count noun, include its conventional indefinite article. Do not answer with a named example when the clue asks for its class, or repeat an embedded synonym that serves only as a cue rather than the target.
edits.content: When the requested taxonomic group has a conventional plural name, use that canonical plural form even if the clue refers to it with a singular demonstrative such as “this.” Do not mechanically singularize the category name; otherwise, match the grammatical number requested by the clue.

edits.target: For a prompt consisting only of a named work, slogan, or quoted expression, with or without a year, infer the intended identifying relation from context rather than defaulting to a definition or classification. When context clearly links the expression to a person or entity being identified, give that attribution; if the prompt asks for the expression's type or meaning, answer that instead. For a quoted catchphrase that also appears in a related work's title, prefer the familiar source work or speaker when context treats the phrase as a catchphrase; return the matching title only when the prompt or context clearly asks for that work.
edits.content: When a clue is framed as “In this book [character or event detail],” treat the detail as identifying evidence and return the book’s title. Do not fact-check or correct the embedded claim unless the prompt explicitly asks whether it is true.

ranking_details.reasoning: Edit 2 adds a useful exception to the existing grammatical-number rule for conventional taxonomic names, preventing mechanical singularization. Edit 0 fills a gap by clarifying that embedded book details are evidence for identifying the title, not claims to fact-check. Edit 1 is narrower and largely overlaps the existing guidance to identify the distinctive shared relation in a list of people.
